article.title: How to Store Fresh Basil So It Lasts for Weeks

intent.main_question: How do I keep fresh basil fresh for more than a few days?

issues.problem: The freezing method is covered in one thin paragraph, while the content brief lists freezing as a required subtopic with expected depth; the article says only that frozen leaves keep 'within a few months' and offers no prep steps, no oil-versus-no-oil guidance, and no notes on using frozen leaves.
issues.why_it_matters: Freezing is the long-term option promised in the article's direct answer, so a reader who scrolls straight to that section cannot act on it and will leave to search again — exactly the unmet-need behavior search engines read from engagement. The gap costs Topic Coverage 1.44 of its 12 points.
issues.recommended_fix: Expand the section to roughly 100 words: dry the leaves first, then either freeze whole leaves flat on a tray (better for garnishing) or chop them into ice-cube trays covered with olive oil (better for cooked sauces); note that texture is lost but aroma survives, and keep the hedged storage window of a few months at a standard home freezer setting.
